articles.title: Peel police investigate after body found in downtown Brampton
articles.summary: Police are investigating the discovery of a body in downtown Brampton. Investigators say the body was located in the Queen Street East and Theatre Lane area, near Tracks Brew Pub, next to some railway tracks. No further details were immediately available, including the age and gender of the victim.

articles.title: Police investigate two incidents targeting Jewish-owned businesses
articles.summary: The Hate Crime Unit is investigating a pair of incidents in which a Jewish-owned bakery chain was targeted overnight. articles.title: Carney announces by-election in three federal ridings for end of August
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced by-elections in three federal ridings for the end of next month. By-elections will be held on August 31 in the Toronto riding of Beaches-East York, Quebec’s Chicoutimi-Le Fjord, and the B.C. riding of North Vancouver-Capilano. The Beaches-East York riding was formerly held by Nate Erskine-Smith, who formally resigned the […]

articles.title: Carney calls August byelection for Beaches-East York riding
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has called three byelections in the B.C. riding of North Vancouver–Capilano, the Ontario riding of Beaches-East York and the Quebec riding of Chicoutimi—Le Fjord.

articles.title: Rally and celebration held after Ford government’s Billy Bishop airport plans grounded
articles.summary: What was initially planned as a rally on Sunday is now a celebration following the federal government’s decision to ground the Ford government’s proposed expansion at Billy Bishop airport. articles.title: A forced-labor crackdown or an end-run around Congress? Dissecting Trump’s new tariffs
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — The Trump administration has imposed double-digit tariffs on more than 60 countries, using a legal justification that permits the president to levy import taxes and other sanctions against countries found to engage in “unjustifiable,” “unreasonable” or “discriminatory” trade practices.

articles.title: Blaze damages 5 homes, displaces residents in Mississauga
articles.summary: Firefighters extinguished a house fire that spread to "several" nearby resident units in Mississauga on Saturday evening, Peel Regional Police said.

articles.title: SIU investigates early morning crash in Etobicoke: police
articles.summary: Ontario's police watchdog is investigating a crash that took place in Etobicoke early Saturday morning, said Toronto police.

articles.title: The Lower Don Trail is reopening after years of delays — but it's not quite finished yet
articles.summary: The section of Toronto’s Lower Don Trail between the Belleville Underpass and Queen Street East will reopen on Aug. 1. The reopening follows years of delays caused by unsuitable soil conditions and weather.

articles.title: Federal government says it won't support Ontario's Billy Bishop Airport expansion plans
articles.summary: The federal government says it won't support Ontario Premier Doug Ford's plan to expand Billy Bishop Airport to allow jets to take off and land there.

articles.title: Police investigate suspicious fire outside Richmond Hill home
articles.summary: Police are investigating a suspicious fire that took place in the driveway of a Richmond Hill home early Friday morning.

articles.title: Victim identified, suspected arrested after fatal shooting in Etobicoke: police
articles.summary: Toronto police say they have arrested a man in connection to the fatal shooting of a 26-year-old woman in Etobicoke Friday morning.

articles.title: Toronto's newest park is getting an expansion the size of 4 Canadian football fields
articles.summary: Just a year after one of Toronto's newest parks first opened to the public, Biidaasige Park is being expanded on Friday to include four more hectares.

articles.title: More than 1,000 scrap tires are piled at this Toronto auto shop. No recyclers will take them, owner says
articles.summary: A Scarborough auto repair shop owner says he has been told by the city to clear more than a thousand scrap tires from his business, but he cannot get anyone to pick them up following changes to provincial tire recycling rules.
